turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
turns.patient_response: I came in because I keep getting stuck on this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek. I notice it in photos and under the store lights, and even though people tell me they can’t see it, it feels like it’s the first thing customers and my managers notice.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent fixation on a tiny perceived facial unevenness that others reportedly cannot see and believes it is highly noticeable to customers and managers.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself spending a significant amount of time checking mirrors, trying to cover the spot up, or attempting to fix it?
turns.patient_response: Yeah. On my breaks I’ll go to the bathroom and check it in the mirror, then try to fix my hair so it covers that area better. I also compare myself to girls who come through my line. Sometimes I lose track of time doing that and end up late getting back to the register.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports repeated mirror checking, arranging hair to cover the area, and comparison with others, which consumes enough time to make her late returning to work.

turns.doctor_question: Deep down, do you feel it's possible that this spot isn't as noticeable as you think, or are you completely certain that everyone sees it the way you do?
turns.patient_response: I’m not completely sure, I guess. When people tell me they don’t notice it, part of me thinks maybe they really don’t. But when I see it myself, it still feels really obvious.
